title: Both components of the projective-line diagonal Chern adjunct
statement:
Let N be a natural number, A a commutative ring with NA=0, and S a scheme on which N is invertible. Put P=P¹_S, W=P×_S P, q:P→S, r:P¹_P→P, and Δ:P→W, using [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change, def-pc-fibre-product]. Work in the ordinary module-derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], with constant objects A_T and finite Tate lines A_T(1) [def-asd-ordinary-finite-p1-kummer-class]. Fix a normalized finite-twist transport t [def-asd-ordinary-finite-p1-arrows]. Let c_S:A_P→A_P(1)[2] and c_P:A_{P¹_P}→A_{P¹_P}(1)[2] have the scalar Kummer realizations of O_P(1) and O_{P¹_P}(1), respectively [def-asd-ordinary-finite-p1-kummer-class]. Suppose the ideal of Δ is invertible [def-pc-divisor-line-bundle], and let c:A_W→A_W(1)[2] have scalar realization c₁(O_W(Δ)), where O_W(Δ) is the dual of the diagonal ideal [def-asd-ordinary-supported-kummer-boundary]. Let p:W→P and e:P¹_P≅W satisfy ep=r, and either p=p₁ and ep₂=P¹(q), or p=p₂ and ep₁=P¹(q) [lemma-nagata-projective-space-base-change-pullback]. Define J:Rp_*A_W(1)[2]→Rr_*A_{P¹_P}(1)[2] by Rp_* of the unit for e, the canonical derived direct-image composition and equality comparisons, and Rr_* of the normalized shifted-twist pullback comparison [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition, def-asd-ordinary-finite-p1-arrows]. Then
u_p ; Rp_*(c) ; J = c_S ; u_r(1)[2] + Adj_r(c_P).
Here u_p is the normalized constant-object unit [def-asd-ordinary-supported-kummer-system], u_r(1)[2] is the shifted twisted-unit component, and Adj_r is the ordinary inverse-image/direct-image adjunct with its constant-object comparison [def-asd-ordinary-finite-p1-arrows]. The conclusion specifies both components before applying any trace; no supported Ext representative or trace occurs in the conclusion.

source.place: Diagonal equation and Chern class of its associated line bundle

proof.text: On the four standard product charts, write the determinant x₀y₁−x₁y₀ divided by the two invertible homogeneous coordinates. Multiplication by this expression maps O_W(−1,−1) into O_W, with image exactly the diagonal ideal. In equal-index charts its image is generated by v−u or u−v; in mixed charts it is generated by 1−uv or uv−1. Coefficient comparison proves these generators are non-zero-divisors over every ring. Hence the map onto the ideal is an isomorphism. Dualizing gives O_W(Δ)≅p₁*O_P(1)⊗p₂*O_P(1). This also covers empty and nonreduced bases.

source.place: Diagonal determinant and degree-one Chern class; global two-component refinement

proof.text: Under e, the two tensor factors become O_{P¹_P}(1) and r*O_P(1), in the order specified by the coordinate alternative. This follows directly from the standard twisting generators: the transition ratio of a pulled-back generator is the pulled-back coordinate ratio. The determinant generators above have the product of these two ratios.

source.place: Diagonal determinant and degree-one Chern class; global two-component refinement

proof.text: Frame torsors of tensor products have multiplied transition units. The Picard-to-H¹ map is additive, the Kummer connecting homomorphism and the scalar-root cohomology map are additive, and both commute with pullback. Thus the scalar realization of e*c is the sum of the realization of c_P and of r*c_S. The roots-inclusion and pure-tensor normalizations in t fix precisely the coefficient comparisons used here.

source.place: Diagonal determinant and degree-one Chern class; global two-component refinement

proof.text: Use the already-stated kummerFirstChernRealization_bijective from Sheaf.Paper.KummerAdditivity (lem-pur-kummer-additivity). Its comparison is exactly ordinaryFiniteClass, not an arbitrary cohomology isomorphism. Applying its injective clause turns the scalar equality into equality of the ordinary module-derived Chern arrows.

source.place: Diagonal determinant and degree-one Chern class; global two-component refinement

proof.text: Take adjuncts. Additivity gives the sum of the two adjuncts. The relative term is Adj_r(c_P). Unit naturality identifies the adjunct of r*c_S with c_S followed by the shifted twisted unit. The composite-adjunction unit equation and naturality of direct-image composition identify the adjunct transported from p with the displayed J composite. The two coordinate alternatives merely interchange the tensor factors, so there is no change of sign.

theorem projectiveLine_diagonal_chern_adjunct (N : ℕ)
    (A : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing A] (hA : (N : A) = 0)
    (t : OrdinaryFiniteTwistTransport A N hA)
    (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : IsUnit (N : Γ(S, ⊤)))
    (cS : ordinaryFiniteUnit A (ProjectiveLine S) ⟶
      (ordinaryFiniteLine A N hA (ProjectiveLine S))⟦(2 : ℤ)⟧)
    (cP : ordinaryFiniteUnit A (ProjectiveLine (ProjectiveLine S)) ⟶
      (ordinaryFiniteLine A N hA (ProjectiveLine (ProjectiveLine S)))⟦(2 : ℤ)⟧)
    (hcS : ordinaryFiniteP1ChernSpec A N hA S
      (by simpa using hS.map (ProjectiveLine S ↘ S).appTop.hom) cS)
    (hcP : ordinaryFiniteP1ChernSpec A N hA (ProjectiveLine S)
      (by
        simpa using hS.map
          ((ProjectiveLine (ProjectiveLine S) ↘ ProjectiveLine S) ≫
            (ProjectiveLine S ↘ S)).appTop.hom) cP)
    (hI : (pullback.diagonal (ProjectiveLine S ↘ S)).ker.IsInvertible)
    (c : ordinaryFiniteUnit A
        (pullback (ProjectiveLine S ↘ S) (ProjectiveLine S ↘ S)) ⟶
      (ordinaryFiniteLine A N hA
        (pullback (ProjectiveLine S ↘ S) (ProjectiveLine S ↘ S)))⟦(2 : ℤ)⟧)
    (hc : ordinaryFiniteClass A
        (pullback (ProjectiveLine S ↘ S) (ProjectiveLine S ↘ S))
        (Scheme.finiteEtaleTateLine
          (pullback (ProjectiveLine S ↘ S) (ProjectiveLine S ↘ S)) N A hA) 2 c =
      supportedKummerChern A N hA (pullback.diagonal (ProjectiveLine S ↘ S)) hI
        (by
          simpa only [map_natCast] using hS.map
            ((pullback.fst (ProjectiveLine S ↘ S) (ProjectiveLine S ↘ S)) ≫
              (ProjectiveLine S ↘ S)).appTop.hom))
    (p : pullback (ProjectiveLine S ↘ S) (ProjectiveLine S ↘ S) ⟶ ProjectiveLine S)
    (e : ProjectiveLine (ProjectiveLine S) ≅
      pullback (ProjectiveLine S ↘ S) (ProjectiveLine S ↘ S))
    (he : e.hom ≫ p = (ProjectiveLine (ProjectiveLine S) ↘ ProjectiveLine S))
    (hcoords :
      (p = pullback.fst (ProjectiveLine S ↘ S) (ProjectiveLine S ↘ S) ∧
        e.hom ≫ pullback.snd (ProjectiveLine S ↘ S) (ProjectiveLine S ↘ S) =
        ProjectiveSpace.map (ULift (Fin 2)) (ProjectiveLine S ↘ S)) ∨
      (p = pullback.snd (ProjectiveLine S ↘ S) (ProjectiveLine S ↘ S) ∧
        e.hom ≫ pullback.fst (ProjectiveLine S ↘ S) (ProjectiveLine S ↘ S) =
        ProjectiveSpace.map (ULift (Fin 2)) (ProjectiveLine S ↘ S))) :
    supportedDerivedUnit A p ≫ (ordinaryFinitePushforward A p).map c ≫
      ordinaryFiniteShiftedLineChart N A hA t S hS p e he =
      cS ≫ ordinaryFiniteP1Unit A N hA t (ProjectiveLine S)
        (by simpa using hS.map (ProjectiveLine S ↘ S).appTop.hom) +
      ordinaryFiniteP1ChernPushforward A N hA (ProjectiveLine S) cP
